head: e6596f44c1e9937050ef68938037f2cf2341ee34
scope: All source AST/symbol inventory plus semantic review of the selected ingestion/derive/read/provider/runtime/memory integration paths; not every line semantically reviewed

findings.title: Staged windows disappear on unexpected enqueue failure
findings.observation: The method replaces self._staged with an empty list before enqueue and only restores on BackpressureRejected; the probe raises before the first durable enqueue and leaves two windows absent. Raw source is not erased.
findings.recommendation: Restore unaccepted work for all failure/cancellation paths; durable discovery must reconcile raw-to-job gaps.
findings.gate: Failure on first/middle enqueue, cancellation and restart: no missing job, no duplicate effects.

findings.title: Direct readiness timeout does not bound inline drain
findings.observation: A 2ms requested wait took about60ms when its inline drain was controlled to take60ms. read.PendingBarrier separately wraps readiness with asyncio.wait_for, limiting that read path.
findings.recommendation: Make the direct API deadline explicit; schedule durable drain separately or enforce remaining deadline without losing accepted work.
findings.gate: Slow prepare/commit and timeout<=0 through both direct readiness and read wrapper; return within defined slack and preserve work.

findings.title: Current window construction still requires generative extraction
findings.observation: Enabled windows require llm.roles.window_extract and construct PromptWindowExtractor; online_extractor without a model returns None. This is current opt-in code, not proof the default silently generates.
findings.recommendation: Reuse segmentation/grounding with a non-generative candidate producer; validate zero-generation profile and required capabilities at startup.
findings.gate: A profile with no LLM role produces grounded allowed candidates/annotations or explicit unresolved outcomes without losing the whole stage.

findings.title: Window prepass annotations are attached through surviving assertion envelopes
findings.observation: The stage derives mentions then iterates envelopes, binding annotations only to cited records and emitting them as envelope extras. This window route does not independently persist successful empty-fact/source annotations; semantic direct extraction has separate mention support.
findings.recommendation: Persist per-source annotation results independently of fact survival, including explicit successful empty results.
findings.gate: Zero facts, rejected facts and uncited source with valid mentions all yield correct source annotation readiness.

findings.title: Raw acceptance and window observation are separate failure boundaries
findings.observation: Raw write handling catches window.observe exceptions and logs them without failing the source write. This is fine for optional enrichment, insufficient for required derivation without durable reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: Pin required work at acceptance; scan committed raw sources into the durable outbox with atomic cursor/job insertion.
findings.gate: Kill/fail after raw append before observation; eventual required job exists exactly once.

findings.title: Open window membership is volatile before a cut
findings.observation: Segmenter/session state is held in the namespace store; outbox payloads are staged when windows close. Durable closed windows do not prove recovery of partial open windows.
findings.recommendation: Persist open membership/source cursor or reconstruct it deterministically from accepted manifests and source versions.
findings.gate: Restart after each of the first five turns of a six-turn window, plus idle/session-close cuts.

findings.title: One namespace window store serialises interleaved conversation/session state
findings.observation: A conversation switch flushes the current segmenter; a session switch treats the previous session as closed. This prevents some mixing but does not implement independent concurrent per-conversation windows.
findings.recommendation: Key active window state by accepted scope/session/conversation or prove equivalent partitioned scheduling; do not falsely close another live visit.
findings.gate: Interleaved A1/B1/A2 with separate conversations and sessions; no false cross-session close or mixed support.

findings.title: Civil source date accepted and naive time can be localised
findings.observation: 2026-10-01 passes normalisation; ingest/write._localize assigns read.naive_timezone to naive datetimes. That explicit old policy is different from the accepted no-invented-timezone target.
findings.recommendation: Define strict source-time validation or preserve unresolved civil text plus provenance; do not invent source chronology.
findings.gate: Date-only, naive datetime, aware offset, generated timestamp and month/year precision variants preserve their supported meaning.

findings.title: Unknown message fields can conceal ID mistakes
findings.observation: An input id field is accepted as an extra while a different message_id is generated; repeating pure normalisation creates another canonical identity. id is not the current supported message_id field.
findings.recommendation: Reject unknown fields in the selected replacement envelope; provide a clear message_id error rather than adding compatibility aliases.
findings.gate: Misspelled identity/time/sender fields fail clearly; accepted identical message_id retries remain idempotent.

findings.title: Name-keyed graph nodes are not identity-safe mention occurrences
findings.observation: Legacy entity IDs are ent:<namespace>:<canonical-name>. The current projector uses record names; source/version/span occurrence projection and stable person identity require additional contracts.
findings.recommendation: Separate source mention occurrences, unresolved bindings, canonical entity IDs and asserted relationship edges.
findings.gate: Two different Alex identities and repeated identical spans survive replay without false merges or asserted traversal.

findings.title: Known-entity prompt context lacks the target evidence manifest
findings.observation: KnownEntity carries name and aliases; _known_from_store builds those from entity/alias state, not the accepted cited claim/source candidate contract. Existing hints must not become authoritative facts.
findings.recommendation: Carry source/version/known-time/visibility evidence through contextual prefill; use current names as hints only.
findings.gate: Later-known alias and erased/revoked sources cannot create unsupported bindings or leak into historical views.

findings.title: Output prefill caps do not bound candidate collection work
findings.observation: Refresh traverses entity aliases and the namespace entity index before prompt selection; cached full-name lists are not equivalent to accepted bounded source retrieval.
findings.recommendation: Bound generation as well as rendering; indexed lookup, resumable cursors and explicit deferred/pruning status.
findings.gate: Large entity sets and many namespaces respect work/memory limits without treating a capped set as globally unique.

findings.title: Live optional fact bundles request at most two source turns
findings.observation: _BUNDLE_TURNS=2 is passed to _source_turns. General claims may require three or more sources for identity, correction, count or time; two selected turns cannot prove full dependency coverage.
findings.recommendation: Build explicit dependency manifests and preserve all required sources or mark incomplete; avoid global count-of-two as a completeness rule.
findings.gate: Three/four-source counts, origin binding plus time, and correction chains retain all required support or explicitly abstain.

findings.title: Benchmarked fitter is not the live Engine assembly implementation
findings.observation: The CPU probe isolates fit_units with exact fixture costs; live compose uses AssemblyPolicy and optional compose.bundles.pack. Annotated links/spans and supplied48-candidate pools make results conditional.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the evidence-bundle contract and validate the actual pure runtime packer against the same cases before claiming Engine2K/3K retention.
findings.gate: Parity on rendered token cost, dependency closure, caps, known-time and inaccessible/missing sources with the actual runtime packer.

findings.title: AssemblyPolicy can admit an oversized first record
findings.observation: The budget rejection branch requires selected to be non-empty, so the first record can exceed budget unless a later configured stage fits it. This is a local policy observation, not proof every final endpoint exceeds its cap.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the selected hard rendered-evidence cap at the final boundary; return incomplete/oversize instead of breaking it for non-empty output.
findings.gate: One oversized record, leading headers, stable prefix and compression on/off all obey the final budget or explicit failure contract.

findings.title: Copied-excerpt erasure policy needs expanded surface coverage
findings.observation: Existing erasure state/lineage/purge machinery is reusable. It does not by itself prove the target20 copy classes, new copied bundles, durable statuses and seven-day backup restore requirements.
findings.recommendation: Integrate new source/copy lineage into existing erasure authority; deny reads immediately and track per-surface physical completion honestly.
findings.gate: Forget during inference, copied excerpts/caches/logs, restart and restored backup cannot re-authorise erased source.

findings.title: Maintenance Temporal runner does not automatically execute ingestion outbox jobs
findings.observation: workers.runner selects maintenance execution; ingest windows use runtime.runner/outbox independently. Embedded SQLite journal recovery also requires accessible persisted storage after relocation.
findings.recommendation: Retain one required-work authority in SQL; register an explicit ingestion Activity adapter after local handler durability is proved.
findings.gate: Activity retries/reopen/reassignment, idempotent effects and journal-volume loss are tested with documented recovery limits.

findings.title: Real GLiNER ingestion evidence uses a deterministic window-LLM fixture
findings.observation: The artifact explicitly says real local GLiNER but window_llm is a deterministic supported-claim fixture. It proves selected real SDK/Engine wiring, not a complete model-free window producer or arbitrary relation accuracy.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the successful narrow gate and add independent non-generative-window/semantic-role tests; do not erase or inflate the historical evidence.
findings.gate: Actual configured non-generative path handles positive and abstention cases with exact spans and zero generation.

findings.title: Accepted typed schema and predicate catalog are not integrated contracts yet
findings.observation: Review JSON and52 mappings remain design artifacts; existing AssertionEnvelope/TemporalRef and producers/consumers still have their current semantics. Runtime helpers with similar names are not proof the coordinated rewrite is done.
findings.recommendation: Freeze BI-01 contracts, then update all affected writers, events, stores, graph/read consumers and fixtures together without aliases.
findings.gate: Structural and behavioural contracts agree for all five synthetic scenarios, typed values, authority, precision and unresolved records.

findings.title: Large uncommitted working tree weakens replay of historical verification
findings.observation: The scan sees615 Python modules and360 Git status entries including277 untracked entries at inventory time. Historical DONE gates do not establish regression freedom for the exact current tree; counts are status history, not a fresh test pass.
findings.recommendation: Preserve a file-hash evidence manifest and review coherent changes; refresh affected focused gates before a release candidate, leaving deferred eval work deferred.
findings.gate: Verification records identify exact revision or working-tree hashes, selected commands, failures/skips and output artifacts.

findings.title: Rules can propose speaker residence from hypothetical or reported speech
findings.observation: The actual parser returns Asha home=Lisbon from If I live in Lisbon..., and Asha home=Porto from Daniel said, I live in Porto. Only the output container is stubbed; downstream persistence is not exercised.
findings.recommendation: Retain quote/reporting/conditional scope and require supported speaker attribution and modality before promoting rule matches. Span overlap alone is insufficient.
findings.gate: Explicit positive passes; quoted, conditional, negated, denied and planned statements do not become unsupported current residence.

review_tests: Isolated current-method probes; no actual DB/Engine concurrency or physical crash injection in this pass
record_kind: Historical review observations at recorded baseline; not a live task register
